paragraphs: ¹⁶ Johanan son of Kareah, and all the military commanders with him, took all the remnant of the people he had rescued from Ishmael son of Nethaniah at Mizpah — after Ishmael had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam — including the soldiers, women, children, and court officials he had brought back from Gibeon. ¹⁷ They set out and stopped at Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem, intending to continue into Egypt, ¹⁸ because they were afraid of the Chaldeans. They feared them because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor over the land.

¹ Then all the military commanders — Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least to the greatest — came forward ² and said to Jeremiah the prophet, "Please hear our request and pray to the LORD your God for this whole remnant, because as you can see, only a few of us remain out of many. ³ Ask the LORD your God to show us the way we should go and what we should do." ⁴ Jeremiah the prophet answered them, "I hear you. I will pray to the LORD your God as you ask, and I will tell you everything he says — I will hold nothing back from you." ⁵ Then they said to Jeremiah, "May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we don't act according to everything the LORD your God sends you to tell us."

⁶ "Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God to whom we are sending you, so that things will go well for us when we obey him." ⁷ Ten days later the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah. ⁸ He summoned Johanan son of Kareah, all the military commanders with him, and all the people from the least to the greatest, ⁹ and said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says — the God to whom you sent me to bring your request: ¹⁰ If you will stay in this land, I will build you up and not tear you down; I will plant you and not uproot you, because I relent over the disaster I have brought on you."

¹¹ "Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you now fear — do not be afraid of him, declares the LORD, for I am with you to save you and deliver you from his grip. ¹² I will show you compassion, and he will have mercy on you and let you return to your own land. ¹³ But if you say, 'We will not stay in this land' — and so refuse to obey the voice of the LORD your God — ¹⁴ and say instead, 'No, we will go to Egypt, where we will see no war, hear no trumpet, and go hungry for no bread — that is where we will live': ¹⁵ then hear the word of the LORD, you remnant of Judah. This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: If you are determined to go to Egypt and settle there,"

¹⁶ then the sword you fear will catch up with you there in Egypt, and the famine you dread will follow you there, and you will die in Egypt. ¹⁷ All who are determined to go to Egypt to settle there will die by the sword, famine, and plague — not one of them will survive or escape the disaster I will bring upon them. ¹⁸ For this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Just as my anger and wrath were poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my wrath will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You will become an object of cursing and horror, a byword and a disgrace, and you will never see this place again. ¹⁹ The LORD has spoken concerning you, remnant of Judah: Do not go to Egypt. Know for certain that I have warned you today. ²⁰ You were being deceptive when you sent me to the LORD your God, saying, 'Pray to the LORD our God for us; tell us everything he says and we will do it.'

²¹ Today I have told you, but you have not obeyed the voice of the LORD your God — not in anything he sent me to tell you. ²² So know for certain that you will die by the sword, famine, and plague in the place where you want to go and settle.

¹ When Jeremiah had finished telling all the people everything the LORD their God had sent him to say — every single word — ² Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah, "You are lying! The LORD our God did not send you to say, 'Do not go to Egypt to settle there.' ³ It is Baruch son of Neriah who is inciting you against us, in order to hand us over to the Chaldeans so they can kill us or deport us to Babylon." ⁴ So Johanan son of Kareah, all the military commanders, and all the people refused to obey the LORD's command to stay in the land of Judah. ⁵ Instead, Johanan son of Kareah and all the military commanders led away the entire remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations where they had been scattered to live in the land of Judah —

⁶ men, women, and children, the king's daughters, and everyone whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, including Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah. ⁷ They went to Egypt in disobedience to the LORD and came as far as Tahpanhes. ⁸ Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah at Tahpanhes: ⁹ "Take some large stones and bury them in mortar at the brick pavement at the entrance to Pharaoh's palace in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah. ¹⁰ Then say to them: This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says — I am going to send for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and he will set his throne over these stones I have buried here. He will spread his royal canopy above them."

¹¹ When he comes, he will strike Egypt — delivering those destined for death to death, those destined for captivity to captivity, and those destined for the sword to the sword. ¹² I will set fire to the temples of Egypt's gods; he will burn them and take their gods captive. He will wrap Egypt around himself like a shepherd wraps his cloak, and he will leave that land unharmed. ¹³ He will demolish the sacred pillars of the temple of the sun in Egypt and burn down the temples of Egypt's gods.

¹ The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews living in Egypt — at Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and throughout the region of Pathros: ² "This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: You have seen all the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and on all the cities of Judah. Look at them — they are in ruins today, with no one living in them. ³ This happened because of the evil they committed, provoking my anger by going to burn offerings to other gods — gods they did not know, gods that neither you nor your ancestors had known. ⁴ Again and again I sent all my servants the prophets, urging you: 'Do not do this detestable thing that I hate!' ⁵ But they did not listen or turn from their wickedness or stop burning offerings to other gods."

⁶ So my fury and anger were poured out and blazed in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, which became the desolate wasteland they are today. ⁷ Now this is what the LORD, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Why are you doing such great harm to yourselves — cutting off men and women, children and infants from Judah, leaving yourselves without a remnant? ⁸ Why do you keep provoking me with what you have made with your hands, burning offerings to other gods in Egypt where you have come to settle? Are you trying to destroy yourselves and make yourselves an object of cursing and ridicule among all the nations of the earth? ⁹ Have you forgotten the wickedness of your ancestors, the wickedness of the kings of Judah, the wickedness of their wives, your own wickedness, and the wickedness of your wives — committed in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem? ¹⁰ To this day they have not humbled themselves; they have had no fear, nor have they followed my law and statutes that I set before you and your ancestors.

¹¹ Therefore this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am determined to bring disaster on you and to wipe out all of Judah. ¹² I will take the remnant of Judah who have set their minds on going to Egypt to settle there, and they will all perish — they will fall in Egypt. They will die by the sword and famine, from the least to the greatest. They will become an object of cursing, horror, a byword, and a disgrace. ¹³ I will punish those who settle in Egypt just as I punished Jerusalem, with sword, famine, and plague. ¹⁴ None of the remnant of Judah who have gone to settle in Egypt will escape or survive to return to the land of Judah — the land they long to return to and live in — for none will return except a few refugees. ¹⁵ Then all the men who knew that their wives had burned offerings to other gods, and all the women who were standing there — a large assembly — all the people living in Egypt in Pathros answered Jeremiah:

¹⁶ "We will not listen to you or the message you have spoken to us in the name of the LORD. ¹⁷ We will certainly carry out every word we have pledged — we will burn offerings to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we used to do, we and our ancestors, our kings and our leaders, in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. Back then we had plenty of food and were well off and suffered no harm. ¹⁸ But since we stopped burning offerings to the queen of heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything and have been dying by sword and famine." ¹⁹ The women added, "When we burned offerings to the queen of heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make cakes impressed with her image and pour out drink offerings to her without our husbands' knowledge?" ²⁰ Then Jeremiah said to all the people — the men, the women, and everyone who had given him that answer:

²¹ "Did the LORD not remember the offerings you and your ancestors, your kings and leaders, and the people of the land burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem? Did these offerings not come to his mind? ²² The LORD could no longer endure your evil deeds and the detestable things you did, so your land became a desolation and an object of horror and a curse — with no one living there, as it is today. ²³ Because you burned offerings and sinned against the LORD, because you did not obey him or follow his law, his statutes, or his decrees — that is why this disaster has come upon you, as you see today." ²⁴ Then Jeremiah said to all the people, including all the women: "Hear the word of the LORD, all Judah who are in Egypt. ²⁵ This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: You and your wives have carried out what you promised when you said, 'We will certainly keep our vows to burn offerings to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her.' Go ahead then — keep your vows and carry them out."

²⁶ But hear the word of the LORD, all you Judeans living in Egypt: 'I swear by my great name,' says the LORD, 'that no one from Judah living anywhere in Egypt will ever again invoke my name or say, "As the Lord GOD lives." ²⁷ I am watching over them, but for harm, not for good. Every Judean in Egypt will die by sword and famine until they are all gone. ²⁸ A small number who escape the sword will return from Egypt to the land of Judah. Then all the remnant of Judah who came to Egypt to settle will know whose word stands — mine or theirs. ²⁹ This will be the sign to you,' declares the LORD, 'that I will punish you in this place, so that you will know that my words of disaster against you will certainly come true: ³⁰ This is what the LORD says — I am going to hand Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt over to his enemies who seek his life, just as I handed Zedekiah king of Judah over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.'

¹ The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah when Baruch had written in a scroll the words that Jeremiah dictated — in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah: ² "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says to you, Baruch: ³ You said, 'Woe is me! The LORD has added sorrow to my grief. I am worn out with groaning and can find no rest.' ⁴ But tell him this: 'The LORD says — what I have built I am about to tear down, and what I have planted I am about to uproot — the whole land. ⁵ Should you then seek great things for yourself? Do not seek them. For I am about to bring disaster on everyone, declares the LORD, but I will at least let you escape with your life wherever you go.'"

¹ The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations. ² Concerning Egypt and the army of Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt, which was stationed at the Euphrates River near Carchemish and was defeated by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah: ³ "Get your shields ready, both large and small, and march into battle. ⁴ Harness the horses; mount up, you cavalry! Take your positions with your helmets on. Polish your spears, put on your armor. ⁵ Why do I see them terrified and retreating? Their warriors are defeated, they flee in panic without looking back — there is terror on every side," declares the LORD.

⁶ "The swift cannot flee, the strong cannot escape. In the north by the Euphrates River they stumble and fall. ⁷ Who is this, rising like the Nile, like rivers swelling with water? ⁸ Egypt rises like the Nile, like rivers swelling with water. She says, 'I will rise and cover the earth and destroy the city and all who live in it.' ⁹ Charge, you horses! Drive hard, you chariots! March forward, you warriors — men of Cush and Put who carry shields, men of Lydia who draw the bow. ¹⁰ But that day belongs to the Lord GOD of Armies, a day of vengeance — vengeance on his enemies. The sword will devour until it is satisfied and drink its fill of blood. For the Lord GOD of Armies has a sacrifice in the north country by the Euphrates River."

¹¹ "Go up to Gilead and get medicine, O young woman, daughter of Egypt. But your many remedies will be of no use — there is no healing for you. ¹² The nations will hear of your disgrace; your cry will fill the earth. One warrior will stumble over another; together they will both fall. ¹³ This is the message the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to attack Egypt: ¹⁴ Announce it in Egypt, proclaim it in Migdol, proclaim it also in Memphis and Tahpanhes: 'Take your positions and prepare yourselves, for the sword will devour all around you.' ¹⁵ Why have your strong warriors been swept away? They could not stand their ground because the LORD pushed them down."

¹⁶ They stumble repeatedly, falling over each other. They say, "Get up! Let us go back to our own people and our homeland, away from the sword of the oppressor." ¹⁷ There they will exclaim: "Pharaoh king of Egypt is only a loud noise — he has let the right moment pass." ¹⁸ "As I live," declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies, "one is coming who is like Tabor among the mountains, like Carmel by the sea." ¹⁹ Pack your bags for exile, O daughter who dwells in Egypt, for Memphis will be laid waste, left in ruins with no inhabitant. ²⁰ Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a horsefly is coming from the north — it is coming.

²¹ Egypt's hired troops are like well-fed calves in a pen — they too will turn and run together; they will not stand their ground, for the day of their disaster has come upon them, the time of their punishment. ²² Egypt flees with a hiss like a snake; her enemies come marching in force and attack her with axes, like woodcutters. ²³ They will cut down her forest, declares the LORD, dense as it may be. They are more numerous than locusts — too many to count. ²⁴ Egypt will be put to shame; she will be handed over to the army of the north. ²⁵ The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to punish Amon the god of Thebes, along with Pharaoh and Egypt, and her gods and her kings — yes, Pharaoh and all who trust in him.

²⁶ I will hand them over to those who seek their lives — to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his officers. But afterward, Egypt will be inhabited again as in former times, declares the LORD. ²⁷ But do not be afraid, my servant Jacob; do not be dismayed, Israel. For I will surely save you from far away, your descendants from the land of their exile. Jacob will return and have peace and security, and no one will make them afraid. ²⁸ Do not be afraid, my servant Jacob, declares the LORD, for I am with you. I will completely destroy all the nations where I scattered you, but I will not completely destroy you. I will discipline you justly, but I will not let you go entirely unpunished.

¹ The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh attacked Gaza. ² This is what the LORD says: "Look — waters are rising from the north; they will become an overflowing torrent. They will overflow the land and everything in it, the towns and their inhabitants. The people will cry out; everyone who lives in the land will wail ³ at the thundering hooves of charging stallions, the rattling of enemy chariots, the rumbling of their wheels. Fathers will not look back for their children — their hands will hang limp, ⁴ because the day has come to destroy all the Philistines and cut off all surviving allies of Tyre and Sidon. The LORD is about to destroy the Philistines, the remnant from the coasts of Caphtor. ⁵ Gaza will shave her head in mourning; Ashkelon will fall silent. Remnant of their power in the valley, how long will you gash yourselves?"

⁶ "O sword of the LORD, how long will you be restless? Return to your scabbard; be still and at rest." ⁷ But how can it rest when the LORD has commanded it? Against Ashkelon and the seacoast — that is where he has assigned it.

¹ Concerning Moab, this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Woe to Nebo — it is destroyed! Kiriathaim is captured and disgraced; the stronghold is disgraced and shattered. ² Moab's glory is no more. In Heshbon men plot her downfall: 'Come, let us put an end to that nation.' You too, Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will pursue you. ³ A cry rises from Horonaim — great ruin and destruction! ⁴ Moab is broken; her little ones cry out in anguish. ⁵ They climb the slope to Luhith weeping bitterly; on the road down to Horonaim there are anguished cries of destruction."

⁶ Flee! Run for your lives! Scatter like a wild shrub in the desert. ⁷ Since you have trusted in your own achievements and your riches, you will be captured too, and Chemosh will go into exile along with his priests and officials. ⁸ The destroyer will come against every town; not one town will escape. The valley will be laid waste and the plateau will be destroyed — as the LORD has said. ⁹ Give Moab wings so she can fly away! Her towns will become desolate, with no one to live in them. ¹⁰ A curse on anyone who is lax in doing the LORD's work! A curse on anyone who keeps their sword from bloodshed!

¹¹ Moab has been at ease from her youth, settled like wine left on its dregs, never poured from one jar to another, never sent into exile. So her taste has remained the same; her aroma is unchanged. ¹² But the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will send men who pour from jars, and they will pour her out. They will empty her vessels and smash her jars. ¹³ Then Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, just as Israel was ashamed of Bethel, in which she trusted. ¹⁴ How can you say, 'We are warriors, men mighty in battle'? ¹⁵ Moab is being destroyed — her towns have been invaded, her finest young men have gone down to the slaughter, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies.

¹⁶ Moab's doom is coming fast; her calamity is approaching swiftly. ¹⁷ Mourn for her, all you who live around her, all who know her fame; say, 'How the mighty scepter is broken, that glorious staff!' ¹⁸ Come down from your glory and sit in thirst, you who live in Dibon, for Moab's destroyer is coming against you — he will demolish your fortresses. ¹⁹ Stand by the road and watch, you who live in Aroer; ask those who flee and those who escape, 'What has happened?' ²⁰ Moab is in ruins and disgraced! Wail and cry out! Announce at the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.

²¹ Judgment has come on the cities of the plateau — on Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath, ²² on Dibon, Nebo, and Beth Diblathaim, ²³ on Kiriathaim, Beth Gamul, and Beth Meon, ²⁴ on Kerioth and Bozrah — on all the towns of Moab, far and near. ²⁵ Moab's strength is shattered; her arm is broken, declares the LORD.

²⁶ "Make Moab drunk — for she defied the LORD. Let her wallow in her own vomit; let her become a laughingstock. ²⁷ Was Israel not a laughingstock to you? Was she caught in the company of thieves? You shake your head and sneer whenever you speak of her. ²⁸ Abandon your towns and live among the rocks, you Moabites! Be like a dove that nests at the mouth of a cave. ²⁹ We have heard of Moab's pride — how very proud she is — of her arrogance and conceit, her pride and the haughtiness of her heart. ³⁰ I know her insolence, declares the LORD, but her boasting is idle; nothing she does will last."

³¹ So I mourn for Moab; I cry out for all of Moab; my heart mourns for the men of Kir Hareseth. ³² I weep for you, vine of Sibmah, with more tears than Jazer receives. Your branches spread to the sea; they reached as far as Jazer. The destroyer has fallen on your summer fruit and on your harvest. ³³ Joy and gladness are gone from the orchards and fields of Moab. I have stopped the flow of wine from the presses; no one treads grapes with shouts of joy — the shouts are shouts no more. ³⁴ The cry from Heshbon and Elealeh is heard as far as Jahaz, from Zoar as far as Horonaim and Eglath Shelishiyah, for even the waters of Nimrim are dried up. ³⁵ I will bring to an end in Moab those who make offerings at the high places and burn incense to their gods, declares the LORD.

³⁶ So my heart moans for Moab like a flute; it moans like a flute for the men of Kir Hareseth, for the wealth they have accumulated is gone. ³⁷ Every head is shaved and every beard cut short; every hand is slashed and every waist is wrapped in sackcloth. ³⁸ On all the rooftops of Moab and in her public squares there is nothing but mourning, for I have broken Moab like a jar that no one wants, declares the LORD. ³⁹ How shattered she is! How they wail! How Moab has turned her back in shame! Moab has become a laughingstock and an object of horror to all those around her.

⁴¹ Kerioth has been captured and the strongholds have been seized. On that day the hearts of Moab's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor. ⁴² Moab will be destroyed as a nation because she defied the LORD. ⁴³ Terror and pit and snare await you, people of Moab, declares the LORD. ⁴⁴ Whoever flees from the terror will fall into the pit; whoever climbs out of the pit will be caught in the snare. For I will bring upon Moab the year of her punishment, declares the LORD. ⁴⁵ In the shadow of Heshbon the fugitives stop, exhausted; for fire blazes out of Heshbon, a flame from within Sihon's former realm — it consumes the foreheads of Moab, the skulls of those warlike people.

⁴⁶ Woe to you, O Moab! The people of Chemosh are destroyed. Your sons are taken into exile, your daughters into captivity. ⁴⁷ Yet I will restore the fortunes of Moab in the days to come, declares the LORD. Here ends the judgment on Moab.

¹ Concerning the Ammonites: This is what the LORD says: "Has Israel no children? Has she no heirs? Why then has Molek taken possession of Gad? Why have his people settled in Gad's towns? ² But the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will sound a battle cry against Rabbah of the Ammonites; it will become a desolate mound, and its surrounding villages will be set on fire. Then Israel will dispossess those who dispossessed her, says the LORD. ³ Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is destroyed! Cry out, daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth and mourn; run back and forth inside the walls, for their king will go into exile, together with his priests and officials. ⁴ Why do you boast about your valleys, about your fertile valleys, O unfaithful daughter? You trusted in your riches and said, 'Who can attack me?' ⁵ I am going to bring terror upon you from all around, declares the Lord GOD of Armies. Every one of you will be driven away, with no one to gather the fugitives."

⁶ Yet afterward I will restore the fortunes of the Ammonites, declares the LORD. ⁷ Concerning Edom: This is what the LORD of Armies says: Has wisdom disappeared from Teman? Has counsel vanished from the wise? Has their wisdom decayed? ⁸ Turn and flee, go into hiding, you who live in Dedan! For I will bring the disaster of Esau's punishment upon him at the time I punish him. ⁹ If grape pickers came to you, would they not leave a few grapes? If thieves came in the night, they would take only what they wanted. ¹⁰ But I will strip Esau bare; I will uncover his hiding places so that he cannot conceal himself. His children, relatives, and neighbors will all be destroyed, and he will be no more.

¹¹ Leave your fatherless children — I will protect them; let your widows trust in me. ¹² For this is what the LORD says: Those who did not deserve to drink the cup will drink it, so why should you go unpunished? You will not go unpunished — you must drink it too. ¹³ I swear by myself, declares the LORD, that Bozrah will become a ruin and an object of horror, a disgrace and a curse; and all her towns will be in ruins forever. ¹⁴ I have heard a message from the LORD; an envoy was sent to the nations, saying, 'Assemble yourselves to attack Edom! Rise up for battle!' ¹⁵ Indeed I will make you small among the nations, despised and rejected by mankind.

¹⁶ The terror you inspire and the pride of your heart have deceived you — you who live in the clefts of the rocks, who occupy the heights of the hills. Though you build your nest as high as the eagle's, I will bring you down from there, declares the LORD. ¹⁷ Edom will become an object of horror; all who pass by will be appalled and will scoff at all her wounds. ¹⁸ As Sodom and Gomorrah were overthrown, along with their neighboring towns, declares the LORD, so no one will live there; no human being will settle there. ¹⁹ Like a lion coming up from the thickets of the Jordan to the watered meadows, I will chase Edom away in an instant. Who is the chosen one I will appoint for this? Who is like me? Who can challenge me? What shepherd can stand against me? ²⁰ So hear what the LORD has planned against Edom, the purposes he has formed against those who live in Teman: the young of the flock will be dragged away; their pasture will be made desolate because of them.

²¹ At the sound of Edom's fall the earth will tremble; her cry will ring out to the Red Sea. ²² Look — an enemy will soar like an eagle and swoop down, spreading his wings over Bozrah. On that day the hearts of Edom's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor. ²³ Concerning Damascus: Hamath and Arpad are dismayed, for they have heard bad news. They are troubled like the churning sea — it cannot be calmed. ²⁴ Damascus has grown weak; she has turned to flee, gripped by panic. Anguish and pain have seized her, like a woman in labor. ²⁵ Why has the city of renown not been abandoned, the town in which I delight!

²⁶ Her young men will fall in her streets, and all her soldiers will be silenced on that day, declares the LORD of Armies. ²⁷ I will set fire to the walls of Damascus; it will consume the fortresses of Ben-Hadad. ²⁸ Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon attacked: This is what the LORD says — 'Advance against Kedar and devastate the people of the east! ²⁹ Their tents and their flocks will be taken; their tent curtains, all their goods and camels will be carried off; and people will shout to them, "Terror on every side!" ³⁰ Run away quickly! Get far from home, you who live in Hazor!' declares the LORD. 'Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has formed a plan against you and devised a scheme against you.'

³¹ 'Advance against a nation at ease, which lives in confidence,' declares the LORD, 'a nation that has neither gates nor bars — its people live alone. ³² Their camels will become plunder, and their large herds will be spoils of war. I will scatter to the winds those who have shaved temples, and I will bring disaster on them from every side,' declares the LORD. ³³ 'Hazor will become a den of jackals, desolate forever. No one will live there; no human being will settle there.' ³⁴ The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, early in the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah: ³⁵ This is what the LORD of Armies says: 'I will break Elam's bow, the mainstay of their power.'

³⁶ I will bring against Elam the four winds from the four quarters of heaven; I will scatter them in every direction, and there will not be a nation where Elam's exiles do not go. ³⁷ I will shatter Elam before their enemies, before those who seek their lives; I will bring disaster upon them, my fierce anger, declares the LORD. I will pursue them with the sword until I have finished them off. ³⁸ I will set my throne in Elam and destroy her king and officials, declares the LORD. ³⁹ But in the days to come I will restore the fortunes of Elam, declares the LORD.

¹ The word the LORD spoke against Babylon, against the land of the Chaldeans, through Jeremiah the prophet: ² "Announce and proclaim among the nations! Raise a banner and proclaim — do not conceal it! Say: 'Babylon has fallen! Bel is put to shame! Marduk is shattered! Her idols are put to shame, her images are shattered!' ³ For a nation from the north will come against her and lay waste her land. No one will live in it — both people and animals will flee. ⁴ In those days, at that time, declares the LORD, the people of Israel and the people of Judah will come together, weeping as they come, to seek the LORD their God. ⁵ They will ask the way to Zion and turn their faces toward it; they will come and bind themselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant that will never be forgotten."

⁶ My people have been lost sheep; their shepherds have led them astray and turned them loose in the mountains. They wandered from mountain to hill, forgetting their own resting place. ⁷ All who found them devoured them; their enemies said, 'We are not guilty, for they sinned against the LORD, the true pasture, the hope of their ancestors.' ⁸ Flee out of Babylon; leave the land of the Chaldeans. Be like the male goats who lead the flock. ⁹ For I am going to stir up and bring against Babylon a coalition of great nations from the north. They will take up their battle positions against her; she will be captured from that direction. Their arrows are like those of an expert warrior who does not return without success. ¹⁰ Chaldea will be plundered; all her plunderers will have their fill, declares the LORD.

¹¹ Because you rejoice and celebrate, you who pillage my inheritance — because you frolic like a heifer on green pasture and bellow like bulls — ¹² your mother will be deeply disgraced; she who gave you birth will be humiliated. She will be the least of the nations — a wilderness, a dry land, a desert. ¹³ Because of the LORD's anger she will not be inhabited; she will be completely desolate. Everyone who passes by Babylon will be appalled and scoff at all her wounds. ¹⁴ Take up your positions around Babylon, all you who draw the bow. Shoot at her! Spare no arrows, for she has sinned against the LORD. ¹⁵ Shout against her on every side! She surrenders! Her towers fall, her walls are torn down. This is the LORD's vengeance — take vengeance on her! Do to her what she has done.

¹⁶ Cut off the sower from Babylon and the reaper with his sickle at harvest time. Because of the oppressor's sword, every one will return to his own people, every one will flee to his own land. ¹⁷ Israel is a scattered flock; lions have chased them away. First the king of Assyria devoured them; then Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon crushed their bones. ¹⁸ Therefore this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I will punish the king of Babylon and his land just as I punished the king of Assyria. ¹⁹ I will bring Israel back to their own pasture; they will graze on Carmel and Bashan, and they will be satisfied in the hill country of Ephraim and Gilead. ²⁰ In those days, at that time, declares the LORD, Israel's guilt will be searched for but there will be none, and Judah's sins will not be found, for I will forgive the remnant I spare.

²¹ Attack the land of Merathaim and those who live in Pekod. Pursue, kill, and completely destroy them, declares the LORD, and do everything I have commanded you. ²² The sound of battle is in the land — the sound of great destruction! ²³ How broken and shattered is the hammer of the whole earth! How desolate Babylon has become among the nations! ²⁴ I set a trap for you, Babylon, and you were caught before you knew it. You were found and captured because you opposed the LORD. ²⁵ The LORD has opened his arsenal and brought out the weapons of his wrath, for the Lord GOD of Armies has work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.

²⁶ Come against her from far away! Open up her granaries! Pile her up like heaps of grain and completely destroy her; leave her no remnant. ²⁷ Kill all her young bulls — let them go down to the slaughter! Woe to them! Their day has come — the time of their punishment! ²⁸ Listen to the fugitives and refugees from Babylon declaring in Zion how the LORD our God has taken vengeance — vengeance for his temple. ²⁹ Summon archers against Babylon, all who draw the bow. Encamp all around her; let no one escape. Repay her for her actions; do to her what she has done. For she has defied the LORD, the Holy One of Israel. ³⁰ Therefore her young men will fall in her streets; all her soldiers will be silenced on that day, declares the LORD.

³¹ I am against you, O arrogant one, declares the Lord GOD of Armies, for your day has come — the time for you to be punished. ³² The arrogant one will stumble and fall, with no one to help her up. I will kindle a fire in her towns, and it will consume everything around her. ³³ This is what the LORD of Armies says: The people of Israel and the people of Judah are oppressed together; all who took them captive hold them fast and refuse to let them go. ³⁴ But their Redeemer is strong — the LORD of Armies is his name. He will vigorously defend their cause so that he may bring rest to the land and unrest to those who live in Babylon. ³⁵ A sword against the Chaldeans! declares the LORD — against those who live in Babylon, against her officials and her wise men!

³⁶ A sword against her false prophets — they will become fools! A sword against her warriors — they will be filled with terror! ³⁷ A sword against her horses and chariots, and against all the foreigners in her ranks — they will become like women! A sword against her treasures — they will be plundered! ³⁸ A drought on her waters — they will dry up! For it is a land of idols, and the people are mad with their horrible images. ³⁹ So desert creatures and hyenas will live there, and owls will make their home there. It will never again be inhabited, or occupied, from generation to generation. ⁴⁰ As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah along with their neighboring towns, declares the LORD, so no one will live there; no human being will settle there.

⁴¹ Look — an army is coming from the north; a great nation and many kings are stirred up from the ends of the earth. ⁴² They are armed with bows and spears; they are cruel and without mercy. They sound like the roaring sea as they ride their horses. They come as a unit, drawn up for battle against you, daughter Babylon. ⁴³ The king of Babylon has heard reports about them, and his hands hang limp; he is gripped by anguish and pain, like a woman in labor. ⁴⁴ Like a lion coming up from the thickets of the Jordan to the watered meadows, I will chase Babylon from her land in an instant. Who is the chosen one I will appoint for this? Who is like me? Who can challenge me? What shepherd can stand against me? ⁴⁵ So hear what the LORD has planned against Babylon, the purposes he has formed against the land of the Chaldeans: The young of the flock will be dragged away; their pasture will be laid waste because of them.
⁴⁶ At the sound of Babylon's capture the earth will tremble; her cry will resound among the nations.

¹ This is what the LORD says: 'I am going to stir up a spirit of destruction against Babylon and the people of Leb Kamai. ² I will send foreigners to Babylon who will winnow her and lay waste her land; they will attack her from every side on the day of her calamity. ³ Let not the archer string his bow, nor let him put on his armor. Do not spare her young men — completely destroy her whole army. ⁴ They will fall down slain in the land of the Chaldeans, pierced through in her streets. ⁵ For Israel and Judah have not been forsaken by their God, the LORD of Armies, even though their land is full of guilt before the Holy One of Israel.'

⁶ Flee from Babylon! Run for your lives! Do not be destroyed because of her sins. It is time for the LORD's vengeance — he will repay her what she deserves. ⁷ Babylon was a gold cup in the LORD's hand; she made the whole earth drunk. The nations drank her wine; therefore they have gone mad. ⁸ Babylon will suddenly fall and be shattered. Wail over her! Get medicine for her wounds — perhaps she can be healed. ⁹ 'We would have healed Babylon, but she cannot be healed. Let us leave her and each go to his own country, for her judgment reaches to the heavens; it rises as high as the clouds.' ¹⁰ 'The LORD has brought about our vindication; come, let us tell in Zion what the LORD our God has done.'

¹¹ Sharpen the arrows, fill the quivers! The LORD has stirred up the kings of the Medes, because his purpose is to destroy Babylon. The LORD will take vengeance — vengeance for his temple. ¹² Raise the battle flag against the walls of Babylon! Reinforce the guard, station the watchmen, prepare an ambush! The LORD will carry out his intention, his decree against the people of Babylon. ¹³ You who live by many waters and are rich in treasures, your end has come, the time for you to be cut off. ¹⁴ The LORD of Armies has sworn by himself: 'I will fill you with troops, as thick as a swarm of locusts, and they will shout in triumph over you.' ¹⁵ He made the earth by his power; he founded the world by his wisdom and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.

¹⁶ When he thunders, the waters in the heavens roar; he makes clouds rise from the ends of the earth. He sends lightning with the rain and brings out the wind from his storehouses. ¹⁷ Everyone is senseless and without knowledge; every goldsmith is shamed by his idols. The images he makes are a fraud; they have no breath in them. ¹⁸ They are worthless, the objects of mockery; when their judgment comes, they will perish. ¹⁹ The Maker of all things is not like these — he is the Portion of Jacob, the one who formed everything, including Israel, his very own possession. The LORD of Armies is his name. ²⁰ You are my war club, my weapon for battle — with you I shatter nations, with you I destroy kingdoms;

²¹ with you I shatter horse and rider, with you I shatter chariot and driver; ²² with you I shatter man and woman, with you I shatter old and young, with you I shatter young man and young woman; ²³ with you I shatter shepherd and flock, with you I shatter farmer and oxen, with you I shatter governors and officials. ²⁴ Before your eyes I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea for all the evil they have done in Zion, declares the LORD. ²⁵ I am against you, O destroying mountain, you who destroy the whole earth, declares the LORD. I will stretch out my hand against you, roll you off the cliffs, and make you a burned-out mountain.

²⁶ No rock will be taken from you for a cornerstone, nor any stone for a foundation, for you will be desolate forever, declares the LORD. ²⁷ Raise a banner in the land! Sound a trumpet among the nations! Prepare the nations for battle against her; summon against her these kingdoms: Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Appoint a commander against her; send up horses like a swarm of locusts. ²⁸ Prepare the nations for battle against her — the kings of the Medes, their governors and all their officials, and all the countries they rule over. ²⁹ The land trembles and writhes, for the LORD's purposes against Babylon stand: to lay waste the land of Babylon so that no one will live there. ³⁰ Babylon's warriors have stopped fighting; they remain in their strongholds. Their strength has given out; they have become like women. Her buildings are set on fire; the bars of her gates are broken.

³¹ One courier follows another, and messenger follows messenger, to announce to the king of Babylon that his entire city is captured — ³² the river crossings are seized, the marshes are set on fire, and the soldiers are terrified. ³³ For this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is being trampled; the time to harvest her will come very soon. ³⁴ Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured us and swallowed us up; he has made us an empty jar. Like a monster he has swallowed us and filled his belly with our delicacies, then he has thrown us out. ³⁵ May the violence done to us and our flesh be repaid to Babylon, say those who live in Zion. May our blood be avenged on the people of Chaldea, says Jerusalem.

³⁶ Therefore this is what the LORD says: 'I will defend your cause and take vengeance for you; I will dry up her sea and make her springs run dry. ³⁷ Babylon will become a heap of rubble, a den of jackals, an object of horror and scorn, a place where no one lives. ³⁸ Her people all roar like young lions; they growl like lion cubs. ³⁹ But while they are aroused, I will prepare a feast for them and make them drunk, so that they shout with laughter — then they will sleep forever and not wake up,' declares the LORD. ⁴⁰ 'I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams and goats.'

⁴¹ How Babylon has been captured! How the pride of the whole earth has been seized! How Babylon has become an object of horror among the nations! ⁴² The sea has risen over Babylon; she is covered by its roaring waves. ⁴³ Her towns are desolate, a dry and barren land, a land where no one lives, through which no one travels. ⁴⁴ I will punish Bel in Babylon and make him spit out what he has swallowed. The nations will no longer stream to him; the wall of Babylon will fall. ⁴⁵ Come out of her, my people! Run for your lives! Run from the fierce anger of the LORD.

⁴⁶ Do not lose heart or be afraid when rumors are heard in the land; one rumor comes this year, another the next — rumors of violence in the land and of ruler against ruler. ⁴⁷ For the time will surely come when I will punish the idols of Babylon; her whole land will be disgraced and all her slain will fall within her. ⁴⁸ Then heaven and earth and all that is in them will shout for joy over Babylon, for out of the north destroyers will attack her, declares the LORD. ⁴⁹ Babylon must fall because of Israel's slain, just as the slain in all the earth have fallen because of Babylon. ⁵⁰ You who have escaped the sword, leave and do not linger! Remember the LORD in a distant land, and call Jerusalem to mind.

⁵¹ 'We are disgraced, for we have been insulted and shame covers our faces, because foreigners have entered the holy places of the LORD's house.' ⁵² 'But the days are coming,' declares the LORD, 'when I will punish her idols, and throughout her land the wounded will groan. ⁵³ Even if Babylon reaches the sky and fortifies her lofty stronghold, I will send destroyers against her,' declares the LORD. ⁵⁴ The sound of a cry from Babylon, the sound of great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans! ⁵⁵ For the LORD is destroying Babylon; he will silence her noisy din. Waves of enemies will roar like great waters; the noise of their voices will resound,

⁵⁶ because a destroyer will come against Babylon; her warriors will be captured, and their bows will be broken. For the LORD is a God of retribution; he will repay in full. ⁵⁷ I will make her officials and wise men drunk, her governors, officers, and warriors too — they will sleep forever and not wake up, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies. ⁵⁸ This is what the LORD of Armies says: Babylon's thick wall will be leveled to the ground and her high gates will be set on fire; the peoples exhaust themselves for nothing, the nations' labor is only fuel for the flames. ⁵⁹ The message that Jeremiah the prophet gave to Seraiah son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, when Seraiah went to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah in the fourth year of Zedekiah's reign. Seraiah was the quartermaster. ⁶⁰ Jeremiah had written on a scroll about all the disasters that would come upon Babylon — all the words recorded here concerning Babylon.

⁶¹ Jeremiah told Seraiah, "When you get to Babylon, see that you read all these words aloud ⁶² and then say, 'LORD, you have said you will destroy this place so that neither people nor animals will live in it; it will be desolate forever.' ⁶³ When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates. ⁶⁴ Then say, 'So will Babylon sink to rise no more because of the disaster I will bring on her. And her people will fall.'" The words of Jeremiah end here.

¹ Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah. ² He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done. ³ Because of the LORD's anger, all this happened to Jerusalem and Judah until he finally banished them from his presence. Now Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon. ⁴ So in the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against Jerusalem with his whole army. They camped outside the city and built siege works all around it. ⁵ The city was kept under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

⁶ By the ninth day of the fourth month, the famine in the city had become so severe that there was no food for the people of the land. ⁷ Then the city wall was broken through, and the whole army fled. They left the city at night through the gate between the two walls near the king's garden, even though the Chaldeans were surrounding the city. They fled toward the Arabah. ⁸ But the Chaldean army pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. All his soldiers were scattered from him. ⁹ He was captured and taken to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar passed judgment on him. ¹⁰ There at Riblah the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and he also executed all the officials of Judah.

¹¹ Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes, bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon, where he kept him in prison until the day of his death. ¹² On the tenth day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan the commander of the imperial guard, who served the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem. ¹³ He set fire to the temple of the LORD, the royal palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem; every important building he burned to the ground. ¹⁴ The whole Chaldean army under the commander of the imperial guard tore down all the walls around Jerusalem. ¹⁵ Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard carried into exile some of the poorest people and those who remained in the city, along with the rest of the craftsmen and those who had gone over to the king of Babylon.

¹⁶ But Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard left behind some of the poorest people of the land to work the vineyards and fields. ¹⁷ The Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars, the movable stands, and the bronze basin that were in the temple of the LORD and carried all the bronze to Babylon. ¹⁸ They also took away the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes, and all the bronze articles used in the temple service. ¹⁹ The commander of the imperial guard also took the basins, censers, sprinkling bowls, pots, lampstands, dishes, and bowls — whatever was made of pure gold or silver. ²⁰ The two pillars, the large bronze basin called the Sea, the twelve bronze bulls under it, and the movable stands — all these articles that King Solomon had made for the temple of the LORD were more bronze than could be weighed.

²¹ Each of the pillars was eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits in circumference; each was four fingers thick and hollow. ²² The bronze capital on top of one pillar was five cubits high and was decorated with a network of bronze pomegranates all around. The other pillar, with its pomegranates, was similar. ²³ There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides; in all, one hundred pomegranates hung above the surrounding network. ²⁴ The commander of the guard took as prisoners Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest next in rank, and the three doorkeepers. ²⁵ Of those still in the city, he took the officer in charge of the fighting men, and seven of the king's advisers. He also took the secretary who was chief officer in charge of conscripting the people of the land, and sixty of the common people who were found in the city.

²⁶ Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard took them all and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah. ²⁷ There at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon had them struck down and put to death. So Judah went into exile, away from her land. ²⁸ This is the number of the people Nebuchadnezzar carried into exile: in the seventh year, 3,023 Jews; ²⁹ in his eighteenth year, 832 people from Jerusalem; ³⁰ in his twenty-third year, Nebuzaradan the commander of the imperial guard carried into exile 745 Jews. There were 4,600 people in all.

³¹ In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, Evilmerodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, showed favor to Jehoiachin king of Judah and released him from prison. ³² He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat of honor higher than those of the other kings who were with him in Babylon. ³³ So Jehoiachin put aside his prison clothes and for the rest of his life ate regularly at the king's table. ³⁴ Day by day the king of Babylon gave Jehoiachin a regular allowance as long as he lived, until the day of his death.
